#* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=April 1 2004|author=Pieira dos Lobos|title=Fern's Story two|newsgroup=alt.magick.serious
|passage=A youngster of my own introduction had been rejected by an object of preadolescent craving and had killed [[coself]] by leaping at the ceiling of co's quarters. '''Co''' was a rising Large Game star, her spring was powerful, our gravity flux was low - co's head struck the surface with enough force to kill on impact.}}
# {{lb|en|nonstandard}} {{non-gloss|[[gender-neutral|Gender-neutral]] object pronoun, coordinate with gendered pronouns {{m|en|him}} and {{m|en|her}}.}}

==Fijian==

===Etymology===
{{rfe|fj}} Compare {{cog|wyy|o|ō|grass}}.

===Noun===
{{head|fj|noun|head=cō}}

# any small non-woody [[plant]], including [[grass]]es and [[herb]]s
#: {{ux|fj|Na '''co''' e vakaveretaka na qele.|The '''grass''' protects the soil.}}
# {{lb|fj|by extension}} any [[herbaceous]] plant

====Usage notes====
This term applies to various types of grasses and herbs, including lawn grass, as well as any small plant that is not woody or shrub-like.

==Macanese==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|mzs|cô|com}}

===Etymology===
From {{der|mzs|pt|com}}. Sense of "and" may be a {{semantic loan|mzs|yue|同|nocap=1}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|mzs|/kɔ/}}

===Preposition===
{{head|mzs|preposition}}

# [[with]]
#: {{uxi|mzs|nhonha '''co''' fula|the girl '''with''' the flower}}
# [[to]], [[at]]
#: {{uxi|mzs|Já gritâ '''co''' iou|t=He shouted '''at''' me}}

===Conjunction===
{{head|mzs|conjunction}}

# [[and]]
#: {{coi|mzs|iou '''co''' vôs|t=me '''and''' you}}

====Usage notes====
* ''co'' is not very commonly used to connect two clauses. More often, related clauses are simply listed one after the other with no connectives, or connected with pronouns such as {{m|mzs|qui}} or {{m|mzs|quelóra}}.
* The Portuguese compound forms {{m|pt|comigo}}, {{m|pt|contigo}} etc. are not used in Macanese. As seen in the examples, "with me" is given as {{m|mzs||co iou}}.

===Etymology 1===
{{etymid|sga|with}}
From {{inh|sga|cel-pro|*kom}}, from {{inh|sga|ine-pro|*ḱóm||next to, at, with, along}}.<ref>{{R:cel:EDPC|head=*kom|page=213}}</ref> Cognate with {{cog|de|ge-||with}} (collective prefix) and {{m|de|gegen||toward, against}}, {{cog|en|gain-}}, {{cog|es|con||with}}.

====Preposition====
{{head|sga|preposition|triggers nasalization}} {{abbreviated|sga|ɔ}} {{+obj|sga|dat|catpos=prep}}

# [[with]]
{{see citations|sga}}

=====Inflection=====
Usually the inflected forms of {{m|sga|la}} are used instead.
{{sga-prep-infl
|3sgm-dat=cono
}}

* {{l|sga|cosind}} {{i|dative singular}}
* {{l|sga|cosnaib}} {{i|dative plural}}

Combinations with possessive determiners:
* {{l|sga|com}} {{i|1st person singular}}
* {{l|sga|cut}}, {{l|sga|cot}} {{i|2nd person singular}}
* {{l|sga|cona}} {{i|3rd person singular}}

=====Descendants=====

===Etymology 2===
{{etymid|sga|how}}
From {{inh|sga|ine-pro|*kʷís|*kʷóbʰi}} or {{m|ine-pro|*kʷís|*kʷódʰi}}.<ref>{{R:ine:LIPP|vol=2|page=463}}</ref>

====Adverb====
{{head|sga|adverb|cat2=interrogative adverbs}}

# [[how]]?
#: {{ux|sga|'''Co'''·bbia mo ḟechtas?|'''How''' will my expedition be?}}

=====Usage notes=====
The adverb is followed by the dependent form of the verb, which is neither nasalized nor lenited.

=====Derived terms=====
* {{l|sga|cote}}

====Further reading====
* {{R:DIL|head=4 co {{m-g|how?}}|9789}}

===Etymology 3===
{{etymid|sga|until}}
From {{inh|sga|cel-pro|*kʷuts|t=to, towards}}, cognate with {{cog|wlm|py|t=to}}. This may be from {{w|Proto-Italo-Celtic|}} ''*kuts'' ‘some (of the) way’, whence {{cog|la|usquam|alt=us-quam|t=somewhere}}, {{m|la|usque|us-que|t=all of the way}}{{,}} and {{cog|osc|𐌐𐌖𐌆|t=as, that|pos=conjunction}}.<ref>{{cite-journal|year=1993|author=Kim McCone|title=Varia II. Old Irish ''co'', ''cucci'' ‘as far as (him, it)’ and Latin ''usque'' ‘as far as’|journal=Ériu|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30006886|volume=44|pages=171-76|accessdate=31 May 2024}}</ref><ref>{{R:ine:LIPP|vol=2|page=439|entry=?''kúth₂-s''}}</ref><ref>{{R:itc:WOU|pages=627-28|head=O.u.puz}}</ref> See {{m+|ine-pro|*kú|t=where}}.

The inflected forms on the other hand are from {{m+|cel-pro||*kʷunkʷe}} ← {{affix|cel-pro||alt1=*kʷum|*-kʷe|nocat=1}}, for which compare {{cog|sla-pro|*kъ(n)|t=to, towards}}.

====Preposition====
{{head|sga|preposition|triggers h-prothesis before vowels}} {{+obj|sga|acc|catpos=prep}}

# [[up to]], [[until]]
# {{n-g|used with the neuter accusative singular of an adjective to form an adverb}}: [[-ly]]<ref>{{R:sga:Thurneysen|p=239|s=381}}</ref>
{{see citations|sga}}

{{head|pl|pronoun|g=n}}

# {{ng|interrogative pronoun}}; [[what]]
#: {{ux|pl|'''Co''' to?|t='''What''' is that?}}
# {{ng|pronoun for introducing a [[subordinate clause]] that narrows the scope of the [[main clause]]}}; [[which]], [[that]]; [[what]]; [[who]]
#: {{ux|pl|Znam takiego gościa, '''co''' ma konia.|I know a guy '''that''' has a horse.}}
# {{ng|pronoun that attaches a [[relative clause]] to the [[main clause]]}}; [[which]], [[that]]; [[what]]; [[who]]
#: {{ux|pl|Ta kobieta, '''co''' mieszkała w tym mieszkaniu, wyjechała do Niemiec.|That woman, '''who''' lived in that apartment, moved to Germany.}}
# {{lb|pl|colloquial}} {{ng|relative pronoun}}
#: {{ux|pl|Jakość będzie równa temu, '''co''' zapłacisz.|The quality will be equal to '''whatever''' you pay.}}
# {{lb|pl|colloquial}} [[why]]
#: {{ux|pl|'''Co''' ona taka smutna?|'''Why''' is she so sad?}}

==Portuguese==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|pt|c'o|co'o||pre-1911}}

===Etymology===
From [[ecthlipsis]] of {{m|pt|com}}, followed by [[crasis]]. Cognate with {{cog|scn|cû}} ~ {{m|scn|cô}}.

===Pronunciation===
{{pt-IPA|cȯ}}
* {{hyph|pt|co}}

===Contraction===
{{pt-contr-adj|f=coa|f2=ca<l:colloquial>}}

# {{lb|pt|colloquial|or|poetic}} {{contr of|pt|com<t:with>|o<g:m-s><pos:definite article>}}

====Usage notes====
Although superseded in the first spelling reforms of Portuguese, the spellings {{m|pt|c'o}}, {{m|pt|c'os}}, {{m|pt|co'a}}{{,}} {{m|pt|co'as}} are often still used in poetic works in order to make the contraction transparent.
